_comment: Values for 32-bit Among Us builds (Steam) that cannot be derived from a
dump. Everything else in offsets.json is read out of dump.cs, computed from
the pointer size, or generated as a signature -- see src/generate.rs.
Keep this file small. Every entry here is a number that will eventually go
stale without anything noticing, which is exactly the failure mode the
_nativeRigidbodyPositionX: Offset of position.x inside Unity's native Rigidbody2D, reached via
Native engine layout, so no managed dump describes it; it changes only when
the Unity version changes. Verified against the hand-written V17.4.0 x86
offsets, which use 124 for x and 128 for y.
_serverManagerTail: Read out of the running game on 2026-08-24. The carried value started at
static_fields + 4, which is null in this build: the ServerManager instance
sits at + 8. Walked live, [4, 20, 8] yields an empty string and [8, 20, 8]
yields "Europe". The instance at + 8 is the coherent one -- its
CurrentUdpServer is matchmaker-eu.among.us, matching that region. The slot
at + 0 also reads "Europe" if treated as the instance, but it is the
DefaultRegions array and its CurrentUdpServer says "Asia".
x64 needed the same correction, and lands on the same rule: the instance is
two pointers into static_fields, not one. 20 is
ServerManager.<CurrentRegion> and 8 is StaticRegionInfo.<Name>, both from
the dump -- only the first hop needed the game, because the instance
belongs to a generic base class whose statics live elsewhere.
_playerControlGameOptionsTail: Vestigial. The client stopped reading playerControl_GameOptions when
newGameOptions was introduced; the key stays so the file shape matches the
_functionPlaceholders: Written straight through. The client overwrites all of these from the
write-path signatures below before using them.
_carriedSignatures: Hook sites for the shellcode AnotherCrewLink injects into the running
game, not addresses of anything the metadata describes. GameReader scans
for them unconditionally on x86, so they have to be present and parseable
even though nothing reads the result while disableWriting is true.
They are not generated, and this is not a gap waiting to be filled. The
client writes a five-byte jump over the hook site and carries the
instructions it displaced in its shellcode as literal bytes --
0x55, 0x8b, 0xec, 0x56, 0x8b, 0x75, 0x08 for the fixedUpdate detour. A
regenerated signature would point somewhere new while the shellcode kept
relocating the old build's instructions. Refreshing the write path is a
change to the client, verified by injecting code into a live game; a
matching signature is necessary but nowhere near sufficient.
Measured against Among Us 2026.8.18 (x86):
showModStamp       1 match      still names its site
pingMessageString  1 match      still names its site
connectFunc        0 matches    the site is gone
fixedUpdateFunc    0 matches    the site is gone
modLateUpdate    162 matches    a bare function prologue, names nothing
modLateUpdate is the dangerous one: it resolves, to the first of 162
sites. With writing enabled the client would patch a jump into whichever
function that happens to be. Validation therefore treats anything other
than exactly one match as unusable and fails the run if disableWriting is
false.
